html:
The Biloxi were a Siouan-speaking people of the Gulf coast of Mississippi, around the bay that now bears their name. Their language was related to the Siouan languages of the Plains, which suggests their ancestors had moved south long before Europeans came.

In 1699 the French explorer Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville met them while founding the Louisiana colony, and the French built a fort, and later the town of Biloxi, on their land. Disease and colonial wars cut their numbers, and they moved west into Louisiana, where they joined the Tunica. The Tunica-Biloxi Tribe at Marksville, Louisiana, gained federal recognition in 1981. Their neighbours included the Houma and Choctaw.
